# Software and Operating Systems

## Core ideas and reasoning

Software is the set of programs and associated instructions that direct hardware. System software includes operating systems, utilities and language translators. Application software performs user tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets and design. An operating system schedules tasks, manages memory and files, controls devices and provides an interface. An interrupt requests attention for an event; the system preserves the current context, services it and resumes where appropriate. Multitasking shares processor time between tasks; multi-user support permits several users to use system resources under account controls. A compiler translates source into target code before execution, while an interpreter executes through translation at runtime; practical language systems may combine these techniques. Freeware describes software supplied at no monetary charge, not necessarily source access. Open-source software grants rights to inspect, modify and distribute source under a licence. Defragmentation reorganises fragmented files on a hard disk; it is not routine optimisation for SSDs. Formatting prepares a filesystem and can remove access to existing data, so backups and authorisation matter.

## Worked practice

### Example 1

Distinguish system software from application software.

System software manages or supports the computer, for example an operating system. Application software performs user tasks, for example a spreadsheet.

### Example 2

Explain multitasking.

The operating system schedules execution of multiple tasks, sharing CPU time so they can make progress. This does not imply that a single CPU core literally executes every task simultaneously.

### Example 3

Distinguish freeware and open-source software.

Freeware can be used without a purchase charge but need not provide source code or modification rights. Open-source licences provide source access and specified rights to modify and redistribute.

### Example 4

Distinguish between a compiler and an interpreter.

A compiler translates a source program into target code before execution. An interpreter translates and executes instructions during program execution.

### Example 5

List four types of system software.

Operating systems, firmware, utility software and networking system software.

### Example 6

Explain job scheduling and interrupt handling as functions of an operating system.

Job scheduling organises tasks for efficient execution. Interrupt handling suspends the current execution to service an event and then resumes as appropriate.

### Example 7

Distinguish between multi-user and multitasking operating systems.

Multi-user systems support more than one user. Multitasking allows multiple tasks to make progress through scheduling. The terms describe different capabilities.
